authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Editing - Formal Execution.md, §V (Versions, Inverses, and the Algebra of Rollback)
note: SPEC vectors for the append-only definition DAG, declared inverses, and three-valued rollback. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: This closes WBD N3, recorded as the sharpest gap in the module.

term_by_term.append-only DAG: RUST-AHEAD, and the reference engine does the opposite. `update_definition` computes `new_version = existing['version'] + 1` and then runs `UPDATE sustain_templates SET spec_json = ?, version = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?` — an IN-PLACE OVERWRITE. The counter increments; nothing is versioned. There is no history table, no parent pointer, and no D_{n-1}.
term_by_term.e⁻¹ (the document): RUST-AHEAD. Nothing in the reference derives an inverse edit — unsurprising, since it has no typed edit `e` to invert (EDIT-2), and nothing to invert back TO.
term_by_term.μ⁻¹ (the instances): RUST-AHEAD, and deliberately partial even here. μ is frequently not injective (Fagin 2007), so the honest answer is three-valued rather than a promise. Neither engine can restore what was genuinely forgotten; the difference is that this one SAYS SO, with Δ naming the dimensions.
term_by_term.three-valued rollback: RUST-AHEAD. R2_BACKLOG #27 records it as not built anywhere. The reference has no rollback of definitions at all — its `control.rollback` is the state-side operator, a different thing.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: The reference DOES bump a `version` integer and stamp `updated_at`, so it can tell you THAT a definition changed and roughly when. That is an audit breadcrumb, not a history: it cannot tell you what the definition was, which edit produced it, or who made it — and it cannot get back.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged; nothing in them is Rust-specific.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. Versioning is a new additive module and touches no existing gate path.

append_only_cases.name: committing_appends_and_the_predecessor_survives
append_only_cases.why: The whole of N3. The reference engine's UPDATE destroys D_{n-1}; here it is still there, byte for byte, after the edit lands.

append_only_cases.name: the_head_is_a_pointer_not_a_counter
append_only_cases.why: Two edits from the SAME parent. A monotonic integer cannot express this — which is the structural reason the article says the version field becomes a head pointer.

append_only_cases.name: a_node_records_the_whole_tuple
append_only_cases.why: ⟨D, parent, e, μ, author, t⟩. An audit trail that cannot say WHICH edit or WHOSE is a breadcrumb, not a history.

inverse_cases.name: the_taxonomy_is_closed_under_inversion
inverse_cases.why: §V's claim, checked kind by kind: AddDim⁻¹ = RetireDim, DropInv⁻¹ = AddInv, and a Modify inverts to a Modify carrying the old value back.

inverse_cases.name: an_inverse_actually_restores_the_definition
inverse_cases.why: e⁻¹(e(D)) = D, applied and compared rather than asserted. A taxonomy 'closed under inversion' that did not round-trip would be a naming scheme.

inverse_cases.name: an_inverse_needs_the_parent_it_was_applied_to
inverse_cases.why: Undoing a DropInv means knowing the expression that was dropped, and only the pre-state has it. This is why the inverse is derived against the PARENT node, not the result.

rollback_cases.name: a_document_only_edit_rolls_back_totally
rollback_cases.why: Nothing about an invariant lives in an instance, so nothing is forgotten.

rollback_cases.name: retiring_a_genesis_dimension_rolls_back_only_partially
rollback_cases.why: μ is not injective: RetireDim forgets, and the dimension's declared default was never recorded anywhere. Δ NAMES it. Reporting this as Total would be the same class of lie as a clamp reported as an admit.

rollback_cases.name: folding_the_log_recovers_the_default_and_upgrades_to_total
rollback_cases.why: The FREE form of 'journal the pre-image': the AddDim that introduced the dimension is already in the history, so μ⁻¹ is a lookup rather than an inference — no extra storage bought it.

rollback_cases.name: an_explicit_pre_image_upgrades_partial_to_total
rollback_cases.why: The PAID form: storage bought exactness for a dimension the log could not account for. A lossy migration becomes losslessly reversible.

rollback_cases.name: genesis_has_nothing_before_it
rollback_cases.why: The base of the DAG is not a rollback target.

rollback_cases.name: an_unknown_version_is_named
rollback_cases.why: A refusal that cannot say which version is an alarm, not a diagnosis.

groupoid_cases.name: each_definition_is_its_own_identity
groupoid_cases.why: The groupoid has an identity per object, not one global identity. Rolling back to where you already are does nothing and restores everything.

groupoid_cases.name: rollback_along_a_path_composes_the_inverses
groupoid_cases.why: Rollback is arrow reversal along a path in the version DAG — newest first, because that is the order the arrows reverse in.

groupoid_cases.name: a_path_is_only_defined_where_the_branches_meet
groupoid_cases.why: e₂ ∘ e₁ is defined ONLY when e₁'s codomain is e₂'s domain — the groupoid is partial, and that partiality is the point. Two siblings have no path between them, and inventing one would be the near-miss the article warns about (a group, where everything composes).

groupoid_cases.name: a_chain_is_no_more_restorable_than_its_worst_link
groupoid_cases.why: One lossy arrow makes the composed reversal lossy. The weakest verdict on the path wins — anything else would let a Total report hide a Partial step.
